title: Twenty-Three Minutes
music: Tense Cold War thriller score: low pulsing strings, a ticking rhythmic pulse, a dark analogue synth drone, a lone piano motif, a deep brass swell, then a warm, hopeful, human resolve at the end, no vocals.
ambience: Low hum of a 1980s underground bunker: ventilation, electrical buzz, faint relay clicks, no music.
next: THE SIR JACK FILES · SPECIAL EDITION
disclosure: Dramatized illustration based on Stanislav Petrov's own interviews and published reporting. Images and motion generated with AI (Google Flow: Nano Banana Pro, Veo). Petrov's lines are quoted from his interviews (The Washington Post, 1999; BBC, 2013) and voiced by a synthetic stock voice; no real person's likeness or voice is used.

sources.name: Pavel Aksenov, “Stanislav Petrov: The man who may have saved the world,” BBC News (Sept. 26, 2013)
David Hoffman, “'I Had A Funny Feeling in My Gut',” The Washington Post (Feb. 10, 1999)
1983 Soviet nuclear false alarm incident (Wikipedia, with its sources)
NPR, “Stanislav Petrov, 'The Man Who Saved The World,' Dies At 77” (Sept. 18, 2017)

shots.say: Near Moscow. September twenty-sixth, nineteen eighty-three. Just past midnight.

sfx.prompt: Night in an autumn forest, wind in birch trees, a distant generator humming, an owl far away

shots.say: In a secret bunker, a forty-four-year-old lieutenant colonel takes the commander's chair. His job: to watch the satellites that watch America's missile fields.

sfx.prompt: A heavy steel bunker door closing with a deep echoing clang
Footsteps on concrete in a long humming corridor
Low hum of an underground bunker control room: ventilation, electrical buzz, faint relay clicks

shots.say: Then, the alarm.

lines.text: The siren howled, but I just sat there for a few seconds, staring at the big, back-lit, red screen with the word 'launch' on it.

sfx.prompt: Loud Soviet military alarm siren howling in a concrete bunker, rising and falling

shots.say: His name is Stanislav Petrov. And the machine is telling him the world is about to end.

ov.kicker: THE SIR JACK FILES · SPECIAL EDITION
ov.sub: A true story, in his own words

sfx.prompt: Distant alarm muffled under a deep cinematic boom swelling into a low drone

shots.say: The system is called Oko. Russian for eye. Satellites, high above, watching for the heat of a rocket engine.

sfx.prompt: Deep space ambience, a low cosmic drone and faint radio telemetry beeps

shots.say: One missile. And the computer rates its own confidence: highest.

sfx.prompt: An analogue meter needle slamming to the end of its scale, an electrical warning buzz

shots.say: And again.

lines.text: A minute later the siren went off again. The second missile was launched. Then the third, and the fourth, and the fifth.

sfx.prompt: Five heavy electrical relays clunking on one after another, each with a short alarm tone

shots.say: The alert changes. From launch, to missile strike.

sfx.prompt: Bunker alarm siren returning, louder, with men's voices rising indistinctly

shots.say: The rules are clear. He reports up the chain of command. And in nineteen eighty-three, the protocol for an attack is an attack in return.

sfx.prompt: Low hum of an underground bunker control room: ventilation, electrical buzz, faint relay clicks
A slow heavy clock tick in a silent room

shots.say: He freezes.

lines.text: All I had to do was to reach for the phone; to raise the direct line to our top commanders, but I couldn't move.

sfx.prompt: A slow deep heartbeat under a muffled distant alarm, slow-motion feel

shots.say: The room is roaring. Maps flashing. A phone in one hand, an intercom in the other. Another officer on the line, shouting at him to stay calm and do his job.

sfx.prompt: Busy bunker control room in alarm: several men talking urgently in Russian, indistinct, phones ringing, teletype clatter

shots.say: But something doesn't add up.

sfx.prompt: Sudden hush: all sound drops away to a single high faint ringing tone

shots.say: One. He'd been told many times: a real attack would be massive.

lines.text: When people start a war, they don't start it with only five missiles.

sfx.prompt: A pencil tapping on a map table, paper rustle

shots.say: Two. The system is new. He has worked on it since the start, and he knows it was rushed into service. In his word: raw.

sfx.prompt: Electrical sparks crackling inside an open metal panel, a buzzing fault

shots.say: Three. The ground radars show nothing. They can't see past the horizon yet, so they prove nothing. But they show nothing.

sfx.prompt: A radar scope pinging slowly in an empty quiet room, wind outside

shots.say: Four. Every alert had to pass twenty-eight or twenty-nine checks. This one passed them all. Too clean.

sfx.prompt: Rapid sequence of small electronic confirmation beeps, one after another

shots.say: Everything on the screen says yes. Everything in him says no.

lines.text: I had a funny feeling in my gut. I didn't want to make a mistake. I made a decision, and that was it.

sfx.prompt: A low tense drone and a muffled siren far away, a slow breath

shots.say: He picks up the phone. Not to report an attack. To report a malfunction.

sfx.prompt: A heavy old telephone receiver lifted off its cradle, a click on the line

shots.say: If he's wrong, the first warheads land within minutes.

sfx.prompt: A loud wall clock ticking in a silent concrete room, slow and heavy

shots.say: Nothing comes.

lines.text: Twenty-three minutes later I realised that nothing had happened.

sfx.prompt: A quiet bunker room settling: a long exhale, a chair creaking, a lighter clicking

shots.say: The cause was sunlight. The sun lit the tops of high clouds, and the satellite read the glint as a rocket's flame. The software meant to filter that out was rewritten.

sfx.prompt: A bright shimmering whoosh like sunlight flaring, ethereal and high

shots.say: There was no medal. Investigators asked why he hadn't written everything down that night.

lines.text: Because I had a phone in one hand and the intercom in the other, and I don't have a third hand.

sfx.prompt: A bare office: a ticking clock, papers shuffled, a chair scraping

shots.say: He got an official reprimand, over mistakes in the logbook. For years, he kept the story to himself.

sfx.prompt: Single heavy rubber stamp thud on paper on a wooden desk
Autumn wind and dry leaves on an empty town street

shots.say: He was the only officer on his team with a civilian education. The others were career soldiers, trained to give and obey orders. He believed any of them would have raised the alarm.

lines.text: That was my job. But they were lucky it was me on shift that night.

sfx.prompt: Distant parade-ground boots stamping in unison, muffled, echoing

shots.say: Machines are faster than we are. They count better, watch longer, and never sleep. That night, the machine was certain. And it was wrong.

sfx.prompt: Modern data centre: dense fan hum and soft electronic chirps

shots.say: In Detroit, in twenty twenty, people believed a computer that said Robert Williams was a thief. He spent thirty hours in a cell for it.

sfx.prompt: Rain on a police car window at night, a distant siren whoop

shots.say: Today, people talk about an AI-centred world. We don't want one. We want a human-centred world, where every machine that matters has a person who checks it, and who can say no. Europe's AI law now says high-risk AI must be built so that people can oversee it.

sfx.prompt: A calm modern office: soft keyboard typing, a quiet murmur of people working

shots.say: Stanislav Petrov died in twenty seventeen, at seventy-seven. In every machine we build, there should be a chair like his. And someone in it. The Sir Jack Files. Case closed.

sfx.prompt: Early morning: birdsong outside, a quiet bunker hum fading
